solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Consuming more rum, English doctor's a feeble sort

indicators.note: the doctor eats the other letters, so they end up inside him

parts.note: DR = doctor, opened up to take the rest in
rum = odd, so more rum = odder
E = English

explanation.surface: A heavy-drinking English doctor is written off as a weakling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink; here it is the old adjective meaning strange, so 'more rum' is ODDER, which goes inside DR along with E.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodderer is someone shaky and frail, a feeble sort.

clue.text: No advantage to be seen in Blue Team

parts.note: blue = down, low in spirits
a side = a team

explanation.surface: A sports pundit says the Blue team has no edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue Team' reads as a club's colours, and blue here is the feeling, not the kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a drawback is the reverse of an upside, so it offers no advantage.

clue.text: A spreading of legs on vacation ruined with despair

indicators.note: a word that has been vacated keeps only its outside letters
the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: LEGS emptied of its middle leaves L…S
anagram fodder with LS

explanation.surface: A holiday ruined, legs sprawled out in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of legs' looks like part of the definition, a spreading of legs; the definition stops at 'A spreading', and legs is emptied to LS for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scattering things over a wide area is spreading them.

clue.text: Bunch of footballers still gaining weight

parts.note: still = ever, as in 'ever hopeful'
a ton is a weight

explanation.surface: Footballers who are still putting on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club, so the 'bunch of footballers' is a whole team.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is an English Premier League football club.

clue.text: As an aristocrat might be advanced

definitions.meaning: a noble title plus the adjective ending -Y, 'like a peer'
advanced in the sense of ahead of time

explanation.surface: A description of how a nobleman might carry himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a made-up word: EARL plus the adjective ending -Y, 'earl-ish'. Only the second half uses the real word.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means before the usual time, advanced as in an advanced or early stage.

clue.text: Is not good to frame House leader? How disappointing!

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture

parts.note: sucks = is no good, in slang

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of House

explanation.surface: A political complaint that the Commons leader is being stitched up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House leader' looks like a parliamentary title; it is just the H that starts House.
explanation.definitionFit: Shucks is an exclamation of mild disappointment.

clue.text: A one-time politician opens shelter — that's fishy

indicators.note: the politician forces the hut open and sits inside it

parts.note: a hut is a shelter
as written
LIB = Liberal, the party the Liberal Democrats replaced

explanation.surface: A former MP moves into a shed, and something smells off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's fishy' sounds like suspicion; taken literally it is the definition, something that is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a twist: 'fishy' usually means suspect, but here it means literally a fish, and the flatfish qualifies.

clue.text: Intimate feature on top of abdomen

definitions.note: 'Intimate' is a noun here: a close friend

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: in a down answer the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of abdomen

explanation.surface: A body part placed intimately on top of a belly.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA is rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so a china is a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a china (plate) is a mate, an intimate friend.

clue.text: Starmer's intitial backing of No. 10 uprising is something out of Shakespeare?

indicators.note: intitial, the clue's spelling of initial, takes the first letter of the name

parts.note: its first letter is S; Keir Starmer is the UK prime minister

indicators.note: backing of means the abbreviation No. is read in reverse

parts.note: the abbreviation No. supplies its two letters

indicators.note: uprising, in a down clue, means the number word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: 10 is ten

explanation.surface: A satirical jibe that the prime minister's first act at Downing Street is pure theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 10' suggests Downing Street, the prime minister's residence, but No. and 10 are split: each is turned round separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote 154 sonnets, fourteen-line poems, so one is a thing that comes out of his pen.

clue.text: Looked back on gutless Trumpite's "Kill!"

indicators.note: back means the word for looked is turned round

parts.note: saw means looked

indicators.note: gutless removes the insides, the guts, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: a Trumpite is a Trump supporter; the outer letters of that word are used

explanation.surface: A cowardly Trump supporter's violent slogan is recalled with distaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' reads as cowardly, but it empties the word Trumpite down to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To waste someone is slang, chiefly American, for to murder them.

clue.text: Nellie's heart put into collapsing boner — 'revolting thing!'

indicators.note: put into means the name's middle is placed inside the jumbled letters
collapsing means the structure falls apart, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the word boner supplies the letters

indicators.note: heart takes the middle of the name, dropping its first and last letters

parts.note: the name Nellie, whose inner letters are used

explanation.surface: A smutty schoolboy line about a woman's passion deflating a man's ardour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' reads as disgusting, Private Eye style, but the definition means rising up against authority; 'heart' keeps all of the name but its two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebellion is a revolt, and a revolt is a thing that is revolting in the sense of rising up.

clue.text: Toby gets wallop on face

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another comes first

parts.note: wallop is British slang for beer
mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: Someone called Toby gets punched in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: Toby looks like a man's name; a Toby jug is a pottery drinking mug shaped like a seated man, so Toby is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toby jug is a traditional beer mug moulded as a figure in a tricorn hat.

clue.text: 'Kindly piss in street,' put heartlessly

indicators.note: in means the word for urine goes inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: wee is a childish word for urine, as is piss

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the middle letter, the heart, of the word for put

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: Someone politely asks people to stop urinating in the street, but says it without any warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is not 'said' here but a synonym, LAY, which loses its centre to give LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindly is an adverb meaning in a gentle, pleasant way, which is how something said sweetly comes across.

clue.text: Dash! Underwear can't expand openings for intimate contact

parts.note: an em is a printer's dash, the em dash
a bra is an item of underwear

indicators.note: openings for takes the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: the first letters of these two words are C and E

explanation.surface: A complaint that a bra will not stretch, opening on a mild oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash!' looks like an exclamation of annoyance but is the typographic dash; 'openings for' takes the heads of 'can't expand'.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrace is a hug, a close physical holding of another person.

clue.text: Fake news: 'HELL LINED UP!'

parts.note: Dis is the underworld in Roman myth and in Dante
lined up = in formation

explanation.surface: A tabloid screams that the gates of hell are opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make it look like a headline; read literally, Dis (hell) is IN FORMATION (lined up).
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: deliberately false reports spread to mislead are fake news.

clue.text: Ignored love wearing gloves

parts.note: love = O, a zero score in tennis
wearing mitts, gloved

explanation.surface: A spurned lover who always wears gloves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like it wants O put inside something; it belongs with 'gloves', and the whole phrase is the adjective MITTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something left out has been passed over, ignored.

clue.text: Crude oil money given to crafty southern Russians?

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters of oil are left in raw disorder

parts.note: the word oil supplies the letters
G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
arch means slyly knowing, crafty

explanation.surface: Wealthy Russians pay sly southerners for crude oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude oil' looks like a single commodity, but 'Crude' is the signal to mix up the letters of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchs are the tycoons who got rich in post-Soviet Russia; the question mark allows the definition by example.

clue.text: They protect members apt to be bent and keep working on head of state

definitions.text: They protect members apt to be bent

indicators.note: working means the letters are being worked over into a new order

parts.note: the word and supplies its letters
the word keep supplies its letters

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the next word

parts.note: its first letter is S

explanation.surface: Pads that let a politician kneel to keep the head of state happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' are limbs here, legs whose knees bend, though the surface hints at members of parliament bending the knee to power.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneepads are protective pads worn on the knees, the joints of the legs that are designed to bend.

clue.text: Political delaying tactic is frustrating shitty act

parts.note: frustrating = blocking
a motion is a bowel movement

explanation.surface: A complaint that parliamentary filibustering is a dirty trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shitty' looks like mere abuse; it is literal, since a motion is also a bowel movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A blocking motion is a procedural motion used to stall business.

clue.text: Mascara melted essentially, sweet

indicators.note: the answer is in the essence, the inside, of the words

parts.note: masCARA MELted

explanation.surface: Mascara running in the heat looks like something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the chewy toffee made from cooked sugar is a sweet, as British English calls a candy.

clue.text: Best to limp off when shafted by one

indicators.note: shafted by means the jumbled letters are pierced by the letter for one
off means gone wrong, not right, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the words to limp supply the letters
a means one, as in a dollar

explanation.surface: Someone hobbles away after being cheated by a lone operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is not I here but A; 'shafted by' drives it into OPTIML, the jumble of TOLIMP, before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal is an adjective meaning most favourable or the most desirable, the best possible.

clue.text: Politician Pence's right to interrupt gentleman and smirk

indicators.note: to interrupt means the politician pieces break into the word for gentleman

parts.note: Sir is the title and form of address for a gentleman
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: right as in the right-hand end, the last letter of the name

parts.note: the name Pence, as in Mike Pence, former US vice-president

explanation.surface: Mike Pence interrupts someone and wears a self-satisfied grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' suggests Pence's politics, but it means the right-hand end of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To simper is to smile in an affected, coy way, much like a smirk.

clue.text: Come by getting accepted by the woman before sexual activity

parts.note: in = accepted, as in 'he's in'
her = the woman
it = sex, as in 'doing it'

explanation.surface: An innuendo about being welcomed into a woman's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come by' reads as dropping in; it means acquire, and the pieces sit in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: receiving property from someone who has died is one way to acquire it.

clue.text: Really keen for it to be like part of the brass section?

definitions.meaning: slang for sexually eager, 'it' being sex

definitions.text: like part of the brass section
definitions.meaning: a brass instrument's name plus the adjective ending -Y

explanation.surface: A trumpet player who is desperately keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is sex, so 'really keen for it' means aroused; the second half turns horn into an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Horny means sexually eager, and horn-y would mean like a horn.

clue.text: Relentless striving produces nation of arses

parts.note: a rat, like an arse, is a contemptible person
race = nation, a people

explanation.surface: Cut-throat competition turns a country into a land of idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'nation of arses' as 'race of rats', then put the rat first.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the endless competitive struggle of working life.

clue.text: Nixon 'hard going' on getting elected? Don't swallow that!

parts.note: Nixon's first name RICHARD with HARD gone
in = elected

explanation.surface: Nixon found the election campaign hard going, and something is hard to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard going' in quotes looks like a comment on Nixon's campaign; it tells you to drop HARD from RICHARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricin is a deadly poison, something never to swallow.

clue.text: Penny has date in America, screwing member of ambulance crew

indicators.note: has means Penny holds what follows, so its letter comes first, then the rest
screwing in the sense of twisting, so the letters are turned into a new order
in means the date letter is placed inside the word America before the twisting

parts.note: the word America supplies its letters

explanation.surface: A woman called Penny has a romantic date in the US with a paramedic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name but is the coin's letter; 'screwing' twists D and AMERICA together.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is a trained health worker who staffs an ambulance and gives emergency care.

clue.text: Brown's disapproving cry on getting in a state

parts.note: MA = Massachusetts
och is a Scottish cry of irritation

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown tuts in Scottish style when he gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown looks like Gordon Brown, the Scottish former Prime Minister, which suits the Scots OCH; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the colour named after the coffee is a shade of brown.

clue.text: King Brian and family impress greatly — gold all round!

indicators.note: the whole thing is turned right round

parts.note: slay = impress enormously
or = gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A fawning report that the King and his family were dazzling and won gold everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls King Charles 'Brian', so King Brian and family are the royals. SLAY then OR, and the whole of SLAYOR reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine-specific name: Private Eye's nickname for King Charles is Brian, so he and his family make up the monarchy's household.

clue.text: Like a bum unknown character having relative breakdown

parts.note: anal = of the backside
Y, an unknown in algebra
sis = sister

explanation.surface: A fussy layabout has a family meltdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative breakdown' reads as a family crisis; the break comes after 'relative', and breakdown means a detailed examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a close examination splits a thing into its parts, as a cost breakdown does.
